newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - SOUTH AFRICA - OCT 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - SOUTH AFRICA - OCT 9.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Toyota Motor Corp of Japan has acquired a 27.8 percent stake in Toyota South Africa in a 446 million rand cash deal, the largest direct investment by a Japanese company since sanctions against South Africa were lifted.

- Higher food prices helped lift producer inflation to 7.4 percent in August from 6.6 percent in July, with the expected increase in the imported contribution failing to materialise, Central Statistical Service figures show.

- Negotiations between South African Airways and the South African Aviation Engineering Union broke down again yesterday afternoon -- prolonging the problems facing the airline which has been hit by labour action.

- The KwaZulu-Natal public works department planned to spend 78 million rand to erect new buildings in Ulundi during the 1997/98 financial year in a move which would bolster the town's bid for provicial capital status, department secretary Jabu Ngwenya said yesterday.

- The government's indecision on restructuring the electricity supply industry was causing a host of problems and could result in South Africa failing to meet electrification targets, National Electricity Regulator chairman Ian McRae said.

- More than half of the underground locomotives at Vaal Reefs mine had been lethally tampered with in the same fashion as the train that caused the accident which claimed 104 lives in May last year, a parliamentary committee heard.

- An official of Sappi Saiccor , the KwaZulu-Natal dissolving-pulp manufacturer, had initiated a campaign to alert prominent international leaders to the "state of near anarchy prevailing across South Africa" and the company distanced itself from the campaign.

- Toyota Motor Corp of Japan has bought the 27.8 percent stake in Toyota South Africa held by Johnnies Industrial Corporation and its pension funds for 446 million rand, or 39.47 rand per Toyota SA share.

- A consortium that includes black business and Times Media Ltd, the listed media group, is set to buy control of Enterprise, the monthly business magazine, from African Life Assurance Co , sources close to the transaction said yesterday. An announcement is expected soon.

- Internal fraud in the insurance industry is so rife that the Hollard Insurance Group now requires selected new employees to take polygraph -- lie detector -- tests, according to Miles Japhet, Hollard's managing director.

- Police have appealed to scores of Gauteng hijacking victims -- who are still able to identify their assailants -- to attend a mass identity parade of suspected hijackers at the Brixton Murder and Robbery Unit.
- Violence broke out between students at the University of Pretoria when a group of mainly black protesters went on the rampage and the second, mainly white, group took action to protect the campus.
